title: 2023 National Film Registry Additions have been revealed.

commenti.body:
Dinner at Eight's cast and crew are stacked beyond belief.  Seems a must-see soon as possible.

Passing Through is at least more feasibly accessible insofar as "films the director's will only screen in theaters and rarely at that" works go than The Ground from a few years back, considering it screens in Califronia rather than Greece.

Fame, I didn't like it myself when I saw it, but I was also in a bad mood and burnt from overwork at the time, so this might be occasion to check it again.

Desperatelt Seeking Susan I know has a massive cult following, to the point pretty much any recommendation of Seidelman's filmography starts with breathless recommendation to start there.  I've only seen Making Mr. Right from her, but it was pretty solid all-round, so I'm curious what her professed masterpiece is like.

The Registry has gone with edge-cases with films produced outside America by directors with American citizenship or whose work had a profound impact on American culture plenty times in the past.  The Wedding Banquet doesn't look all that odd an inclusion in the company of Lawrence of Arabia and The Devil Never Sleeps.

I was somehow unaware of the Hoop Dreams controversy.  At least it and the Maya Lin film are now equals within the Registry, no need for further competition.

I'm just always happy when home movies and student films make the Registry.  Really underscores the breadth of who can make cinema and what contains value that they can sit alongside the likes of T2 and Home Alone as essential to the American filmic spirit.

My happiness at Nightmare finally getting in is tempered somewhat by disappointment at the Library's continued passing over any animated film not from Disney in favor of two animated features from them this year.  Get some Richard Williams in, ya cowards.  Raggedy Ann or bust.

I’ve generally thought of the National Film Registry as choosing films that, despite their apparent quality, are exemplary of some aspect of American culture or history. For example, I didn’t at all enjoy Bamboozled, I thought it was poorly filmed, and the writing was hamfisted and obvious, yet the conversation the film sparks is a deeply interesting one, and it’s one of the few films to delve into such topics, so I feel it fits the bill. Same goes for Desperately Seeking Susan. It’s not my cup of tea, but it’s a very effective distillation of a particular time and place in American culture. The film I’m most stoked to see on the list is Matewan. Wonderful film about a period of American labor history that should be thought more. John Sayles is seriously one of the most under-appreciated (in the mainstream) American filmmakers ever.

It’s weird to see a film like 12 Years a Slave in this early, but if it had to be any film from 2013 that one makes the most sense.

Wasn’t sure if Home Alone would ever get added, given it’s a very mainstream film that isn’t regarded as a masterpiece or anything. But it undoubtably is important to culture.

Terminator 2 is well overdue. Surprised they added it considering their usual hesitance on adding sequels.

Socked at Bamboozled too considering it’s not one of Spike Lee’s most well regarded films, but it may be because of the conversation it stirs up.

Lady and the Tramp and Nightmare Before Christmas… okay, Nightmare being included is cool and all, but I wish they’d add an animated film that wasn’t Disney. Hell I wish they’d add more independent animated films, like the works of Ralph Bakshi (Fritz the Cat in particular, given how it basically pushed in a renaissance of adult animation). The only one added that’s been added that’s not Disney is Shrek. I know they need popular films to make headlines, but now that they’re adding more than one animated movie a year they could add one popular and one experimental one. One for headlines, one not.

Overall a lot of surprises this year. Lot of good stuff. Just wish the animation representation was better.

Love and basketball being added is suprising. I always thought of that movie as only being loved within the black community. I am happy to see it here though.

Home Alone has stayed important to American cinema and American culture in general for time now. It's truly a great example of how much staying power a movie can have. 

Terminator II. I am suprised that one isn't on the registry already.
Yes more animation needs to be added. I can definitely see something like a Toy Story being added!
Toy Story got added years ago. I could see the sequels also being added though
Toy story got in 2005 its first year of eligibility
